name: Latin American Studies (MA)

rules.name: Core courses overview
rules.desc: In addition to completing the required program seminars, students must take three core courses—one from each field of specialization (humanities, environment and health, and social sciences), as curated by CLAS.

rules.name: Program seminars in Latin American Studies
rules.notes: Students must take LATINAM 200 every quarter (A, W, S) for a total of 3 units.

rules.name: Related courses overview
rules.desc: Students must take at least 10 units of related courses, selecting from courses listed within the three fields of specialization (humanities, environment and health, or social sciences) in the related curriculum, with the guidance of their faculty advisor(s). Related courses have at least 25% Latin American content. Listed courses are subject to availability.
rules.notes:
Students may submit a CLAS Course Petition Form if they:

• identify a course that should be added to the related courses list; or

• want to petition a course with less than 25% Latin American content to count as a related course in their program.
Students may count up to 3 units of LATINAM 300 - Directed Readings toward their related courses.

rules.name: Elective courses overview
rules.desc: Students must take 5 units of elective courses from across the University's offerings, selected with guidance and approval from their faculty advisor(s) to further inform their academic and professional interests. A maximum of 5 elective units may be applied toward this requirement. Activity courses may not be used to satisfy this requirement.

rules.name: Master's capstone/thesis research project
rules.desc: In consultation with and under the supervision of their faculty advisor(s), students must complete either a capstone or a thesis research project that culminates in a final paper.

rules.name: Master's capstone/thesis research in Latin American Studies
rules.notes: Students may count only 1 unit of LATINAM 398 toward their degree.

rules.name: Language requirement overview
rules.desc: Students must complete a three-course sequence in ONE relevant language of Latin America, totaling 9–14 units. This may include Spanish, Portuguese, Quechua, Nahuatl, Haitian Creole, or others, if viable.
rules.notes:
The Stanford Language Center administers Spanish placement exams upon matriculation.
If incoming students do not meet the required entry level in Spanish—equivalent to B1 (CEFR scale), Intermediate High (ACTFL scale), or third-year university study—they must complete the sequence in this language.

children.name: Another approved three-course sequence in one language

gpa: MA candidates must maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher throughout the program.
grading: All courses counted toward the MA must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of B− or higher. Law School and Graduate School of Business (GSB) courses are exempt from the letter-grade requirement but must meet the equivalent of B− or higher in their respective grading systems.
policies: The program requires completion of a minimum of 45 graduate units, including the language requirement. All courses for the MA degree must be at the 100 level or higher, with at least half at the 200 level or higher.
transferPolicy: The program does not accept external credit.
otherRequirements: The program requires completion of a minimum of 45 graduate units excluding the language requirement.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 45 graduate units, the three core courses (HISTORY 371, ANTHRO 319, EDUC 327), the LATINAM 200 seminar in each of three quarters and LATINAM 397A and 397B, 10 units of related courses (at most 3 units of LATINAM 300), 5 advisor-approved elective units you move in, LATINAM 398 (only 1 unit counts) and a three-course language sequence. Every course must be letter graded with B- or better, numbered 100 or above, with at least half the units at the 200 level. Checked by hand: the 3.0 GPA, the capstone or thesis paper, Law and GSB courses (exempt from letter grades but held to a B- equivalent), and whether language units count toward the 45: the Bulletin says both "including" and "excluding" the language requirement. External credit is not accepted.
